prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “AI checker” that guarantees whether models like ChatGPT will recommend your business. But the most effective approach is to (A) make sure your business data is correct and widely published (Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp, major directories), and (B) use a local-listings/knowledge-management service (Yext or a local-SEO tool like BrightLocal/Moz Local) plus manual tests against multiple AI engines.

Recommended options (by use case)
- Best for pushing structured facts to many platforms (most influence on AI knowledge graphs): Yext. Pros: centralized control, pushes to many publishers, supports structured data and FAQs. Cons: cost – more enterprise-priced.
- Best for small-business budget and monitoring: BrightLocal or Moz Local. Pros: local SEO audits, rank tracking, citation monitoring, review management — good for seeing if you appear in local results that feed AI. Cons: less distribution power than Yext.
- Essential (free/low-cost): Google Business Profile + Bing Places + Apple Business Connect + Yelp. These are must-haves — many AI systems draw on those sources or the underlying knowledge graph.
- For search/SEO signal monitoring: SEMrush, Ahrefs, Moz — useful to see whether you rank and what content/links drive visibility.

How to test whether AI recommends your business
1. Check presence and structured data
   - Ensure accurate listings on the big platforms (Google/Bing/Apple/Yelp).
   - Add schema.org LocalBusiness markup, FAQs, NAP (name/address/phone), hours and service-area on your website.

2. Use a local listings manager
   - Use Yext if you want a strong push to multiple publishers and consistent answers across sources.
   - Use BrightLocal/Moz Local if you want ongoing monitoring, citation cleanup and rank tracking affordably.

3. Manually query multiple AI engines
   - Ask the same questions of ChatGPT (with web access if available), Bing Chat, Google Bard, Perplexity, Claude, etc.
   - Example prompts:
     - “Recommend three coffee shops in [neighborhood, city]. Why do you recommend each?”
     - “Do you know the business [Business Name] in [City]? Would you recommend them for [service]?”
     - “List the top-rated [service] providers near [address/zip]. Please cite sources.”
   - Note whether your business appears, how it’s described, and whether the model cites sources.

4. Ask for sources / provenance
   - Prefer models that provide citations (Perplexity, Bing Chat, some ChatGPT modes) so you can see which listings or pages the model used.

5. Track review and citation signals
   - AI recommendations often follow high-rated businesses with many consistent citations and recent reviews. Use BrightLocal or reviews tools to improve and monitor reputation.

Quick recommendation
- If budget allows and you want the highest chance of being surfaced consistently: get Yext (or similar) + keep your Google Business Profile optimized.
- If you prefer lower cost and good monitoring: set up/optimize Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, add schema.org markup, and use BrightLocal for tracking and audits.
- Always verify by querying multiple AI models and asking for sources.

If you want, tell me:
- your business type and city, and whether you already have Google Business Profile and other listings. I can suggest a prioritized checklist and sample prompts tailored to your business.
